newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: SKorea POSCO's offer to buy Hanbo assets.
newsitem.headline: SKorea POSCO's offer to buy Hanbo assets.

text.p: South Korea's Pohang Iron and Steel Co (POSCO) and Dong Kuk Steel Mill Co Ltd will offer to buy Hanbo Steel Co's assets at Tuesday's auction by Hanbo's creditors, POSCO said on Monday.

"To avoid disputes in international trade and in debt repayment which could rise from taking over the shares, we have decide to propose buying the assets," POSCO, the nation's largest steel-maker said in a statement.
Hanbo's creditors called a second auction for Tuesday to sell off Hanbo Steel which collapsed in January under an estimated debt of five trillion won.
POSCO said although Dong Kuk Steel was considering taking over Hanbo Steel, the company was not large enough to purchase Hanbo alone.

POSCO suggested that Dong Kuk buy a section of Hanbo's steel mill which produced hot-rolled steel and iron rods, and that POSCO form a consortium to buy a mill still being built, which is based on an electric furnace.

The number one steel-maker said it had originally planned to stay out of the auction of Hanbo Steel but decided that the delay in the completion of Hanbo's mill could cause a loss to the entire steel industry in South Korea.
The giant Hyundai Group has publicly said it is not interested in the purchase of Hanbo, even though it has pressed the government for permission to build a traditional blast furnace.
Electric furnaces are more energy efficient than blast furnaces but produces steel of lesser quality.
